paper_metadata.title: Excellent ductility and serration feature of metastable CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy at extremely low temperatures

evidence.quote: a face-centered-cubic (FCC) CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy (HEA) with great ductility is investigated under the cryogenic environment.
In this study, the low-SFE FCC CoCrFeNi HEA exhibits an excellent combination of high strength and high ductility at extremely low temperatures.

evidence.quote: hot-forged at 1,473 K more than six times to ensure the chemical homogeneity and to eliminate the casting flaws, and then cooled to RT in air. The final dimensions are 30 mm in thickness and 60 mm in width (a total reduction in thickness of about 62.5%).

Rectangular dog-bone shaped tensile specimens with a gauge length of 15 mm were machined from the ingot by electrical discharge machining (EDM). Both sides of the specimen were ground using the SiC paper, resulting in a final thickness of about 1.7 mm and a gauge width of about 3 mm.

evidence.section: Serration mechanism and the difference between CoCrFeNi and stainless steel
evidence.quote: the typical bright-field STEM image and SAED pattern of [110]FCC||[1120] HCP (inset in Fig. 6g) indicate the twinning and HCP phase.

The twins at nanoscale have the thickness ranging from 10 to 200 nm. They reside within the larger annealing twins, which are present in the original sample before the tensile test, and sometimes penetrate across the pre-existing twin boundaries, as seen inFig. 6d.

evidence.section: Serration mechanism and the difference between CoCrFeNi and stainless steel
evidence.quote: The combined effect of the predominant twinning deformation and FCC→HCP phase transformation results in the superior mechanical properties of CoCrFeNi at 4.2 K.

The deformation twinning together with phase transformation at liquid helium temperature produces an adequate strain-hardening rate that sustains the stable plastic flow at high stresses, resulting in the serration feature.
